14                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

15   Resolution Number 783, by Senator Amedore, 

16   honoring Emma Detlefsen for her outstanding 

17   advocacy, support, and fundraising efforts for 

18   lymphedema awareness.

19                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

20   Amedore.

21                SENATOR AMEDORE:   Mr. President, 

22   thank you for allowing this great introduction 

23   of this fine superhero that I have next to me 

24   here.  Her name is Emma Detlefsen, and her 

25   family joins us here this morning.  


                                                                616

 1                Emma took the challenge for raising 

 2   money and awareness for a very special cause 

 3   that she so passionately believes in.  At the 

 4   age of 6, a first-grader, she had a team of 

 5   people, of friends and families, who walked 

 6   across the Brooklyn Bridge to raise money and 

 7   awareness for lymphedema.  

 8                And she believes that raising money 

 9   and advocating for this terrible disease -- 

10   which she has -- she believes that, in time, 

11   research can be developed to finally cure this 

12   disease.

13                So I want to recognize Emma, our 

14   superhero this morning.  To be in her presence 

15   and in all of her great graces, that she is 

16   working so hard for so many fine New Yorkers who 

17   are suffering from lymphedema and lymphatic 

18   diseases, that she is our superhero today in the 

19   State Senate.  

20                And, Mr. President, please 

21   recognize her and her family:  Her mother, 

22   Tiffany; her father, Nicholas; and her superhero 

23   brother Jacob.

 8                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 9   Resolution Number 577, by Senator Kennedy, paying 

10   tribute to the life, accomplishments and music of 

11   renowned rhythm and blues singer Lance Diamond.  

12                "WHEREAS, It is with regret and 

13   sorrow that this Legislative Body records the 

14   passing of Buffalo, New York, music legend Lance  

15   Diamond, noting the loss of an individual whose 

16   hard work and dedication helped to bridge the 

17   massive chasm between lounge music, old school 

18   rhythm and blues, Vegas-style soul and gritty 

19   punk-pop; and 

20                "WHEREAS, Lance Diamond of Buffalo, 

21   New York, died on Sunday, January 4, 2015, at the 

22   age of 81; a musical tribute celebrating his life 

23   was held on Friday, January 9, 2015; and 

24                "WHEREAS, In 1970, Lance Diamond 

25   began his illustrious career performing with the 


                                                                620

 1   Pneu Breed band; for many years he toured the 

 2   United States and Japan with Isaac and the Lance 

 3   Diamond Show, opening for such stars as James 

 4   Brown and The Righteous Brothers; and 

 5                "WHEREAS, Nicknamed 'the 

 6   hardest-working man in Buffalo show business,' 

 7   Lance Diamond was inducted into the prestigious 

 8   Buffalo Music Hall of Fame in 1992; he was also 

 9   the recipient of many local music awards; and 

10                "WHEREAS, In a career which spanned 

11   more than four decades, Lance Diamond and his 24 

12   Karat Diamond Band appeared at every major local 

13   festival and public event; his dynamic 

14   personality, his deep croon and his dance rhythms 

15   always entertained his adoring audience; and 

16                "WHEREAS, Among Lance Diamond's many 

17   fans were the Goo Goo Dolls, who included him on 

18   their recordings and performed live with him on 

19   many occasions; in recent years, he also hosted a 

20   Saturday night radio show; and 

21                "WHEREAS, Lance Diamond 

22   distinguished himself in his profession and by 

23   his sincere dedication and substantial 

24   contribution to the welfare of his community; and 

25                "WHEREAS, Lance Diamond's commitment 


                                                                621

 1   to excellence, and his spirit of humanity,  

 2   carried over into all fields of enterprise,   

 3   including charitable and civic endeavors; and 

 4                "WHEREAS, Lance Diamond was an 

 5   impassioned advocate for Music is Art, an  

 6   organization dedicated to exploring and reshaping 

 7   music's cultural, social, and educational impact 

 8   on our communities; and 

 9                "WHEREAS, Fellow musicians recall 

10   Lance Diamond's heartfelt motto:  'Give the same 

11   for a crowd of three people as you would for 

12   30,000, and give it appreciatively'; he leaves 

13   behind a legacy which will long endure the 

14   passage of time and will remain as a comforting  

15   memory to all he served and befriended; now, 

16   therefore, be it 

17                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

18   Body pause in its deliberations to pay tribute to 

19   the life, accomplishments and music of renowned 

20   rhythm and blues singer Lance Diamond; and be it 

21   further 

22                "RESOLVED, That a copy of this 

23   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

24   the family of Lance Diamond."

25                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 


                                                                622

 1   Kennedy.

 2                SENATOR KENNEDY:   Thank you very 

 3   much, Mr. President.

 4                It's with great honor and pride that 

 5   I rise to remember the life, contribution and 

 6   legacy of a musical icon and irreplaceable legend 

 7   in Buffalo, Western New York, New York State, and 

 8   across this great country:  Lance Diamond.  

 9                I'd like to recognize Lance 

10   Diamond's sister, Paulette Counts, who came all 

11   the way up from Buffalo, New York, this morning 

12   to be with us today as we pay tribute to the life 

13   and accomplishments of her brother.

14                While we're saddened by the loss of 

15   a person who brought us so much entertainment and 

16   joy, we're grateful for the opportunity to have 

17   shared in those memories as a community and to 

18   really preserve his legacy.  See, Lance Diamond 

19   was an icon in Western New York, in the City of 

20   Buffalo.  His personality was as big as this 

21   state.  His personality was one of love -- love 

22   for people, love for entertainment, and love for 

23   the City of Buffalo.

24                He grew in stature and his 

25   entertainment touched so many lives that he 


                                                                623

 1   actually was offered opportunities to play 

 2   outside of Buffalo and Western New York to the 

 3   highest entertainment hotspot in the land, 

 4   Las Vegas -- and he turned it down.  Why?  

 5   Because he loved Buffalo.  He loved Buffalo, he 

 6   loved Western New York, he loved New York State, 

 7   and he loved the people.  

 8                And that's what his entertainment 

 9   was all about.  In the brief conversation I had 

10   with his sister Paulette this morning, she said, 

11   "You know what, we were brought up to respect 

12   other people, to respect ourselves, and really to 

13   love one another."  

14                And that's what he did.  He exuded 

15   this confidence and this presence, so other 

16   musical icons became attached to him.  The 

17   Goo Goo Dolls, that are some of Buffalo's best, 

18   they have gone on to gold and platinum records 

19   across the nation, across the globe -- they 

20   played with Lance Diamond.  He played with them.  

21   They played off of one another.  

22                The Goo Goo Dolls paid tribute to 

23   the life and accomplishments of Lance Diamond at 

24   his funeral and said that they grew into the band 

25   that they are because Lance Diamond gave them so 


                                                                624

 1   much to help them grow, as individuals and 

 2   collectively.  

 3                That's the sort of person Lance 

 4   Diamond was.  But his entertainment, his 

 5   entertainment is what made him thrive.

 6                You know, he had the 24 Karat Band.  

 7   And anybody that ever saw Lance Diamond -- and 

 8   you'd be hard-pressed to find anyone in Western 

 9   New York who hadn't seen him entertain -- knew 

10   that when you saw Lance Diamond entertaining, he 

11   would put on a show of all shows.  He'd entertain 

12   the crowd, he'd get the folks engaged in the 

13   crowd, he'd do a little bit of ribbing, he'd pull 

14   people in, and he'd show off his 24-carat 

15   bracelet that was just such an icon as part of 

16   this legendary icon himself.

17                He was a mainstay at the Elmwood 

18   Lounge in Buffalo that is still a house of jazz 

19   but was often referred to with great reverence as 

20   "the house that Lance built."  

21                And with summer coming upon us -- 

22   well, it might not seem like it outside, but the 

23   clock is ticking fast -- we're going to have 

24   festivals and concerts all throughout Buffalo and 

25   Western New York.  And they certainly will not be 


                                                                625

 1   the same without Lance Diamond, although his 

 2   personality, his entertainment, and his legend 

 3   will absolutely persevere in Western New York, 

 4   with people in our community as well as the 

 5   entertainers that will certainly be working 

 6   simply to carry out his legend.

 7                We're truly grateful for all that 

 8   he's done for our community and for sharing his 

 9   gifts, his talents and his entertainment with us 

10   for so many years.  Lance Diamond will be missed 

11   by all of us.  May he rest in peace.

12                Thank you, Mr. President.

17   as eloquently as Senator Kennedy did on this

21   Diamond, he was an amazing performer and 

22   entertainer.  He had a love of live and for the

24                My wife and I would always have 

25   friends in from out of town; her family is from 


                                                                626

 1   all over the country.  And when they would come 

 2   to Buffalo, they would want chicken wings, a 

 3   Bills game, and a Lance Diamond show.  

 4                And when my brother-in-law in 

 5   California, you know, saw Lance passed away, he 

 6   was one of the first persons to reach out to us.  

 7   And it's really -- it's an iconic figure that we 

 8   lose in Western New York.  

 9                And so my heart goes out to his 

10   family.  And, you know, we lost a great artist.  

11   So I echo much of what Senator Kennedy had to 

12   say.  

13                Thank you.

 3                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative

 6   proclaim February 28, 2015, as Rare Disease 

 7   Awareness Day in the State of New York.

 8                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 9   Hannon.

10                SENATOR HANNON:   Thank you, 

11   Mr. President.

12                This week probably is Health Week, 

13   with so many different people involved in the 

14   healthcare system in New York visiting us here in 

15   the Capitol.  

16                And it's appropriate that we have a 

17   resolution in regard to National Rare Disease 

18   Day.  It began as a movement in Europe, it's 

19   flowered right here in the capital, where the 

20   Albany Medical Center and College has established 

21   the Rare Disease Forum.

22                There are over 7,000 rare diseases 

23   in the world, many of which don't get the 

24   attention they deserve.  By recognizing those 

25   diseases through the resolution, by recognizing 


                                                                628

 1   Albany Med through its forum, we can give people 

 2   who suffer from these diseases hope that there 

 3   will be attention to them, that there will be 

 4   resources for them, that there will be research 

 5   on it, and encourage pharmaceutical companies and 

 6   other researchers in the medical field to pay 

 7   attention.  

 8                So I'm happy to move that this 

 9   resolution, previously adopted, be continued to 

10   be adopted.
